title: SIG questionnaire walkthrough - Cedar Bank
meeting_header:
Date: 2025-11-05 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: ~56 minutes
Redwood: Marcus Lee (AE), Priya Shah (SE), Oliver Grant (CSM)
Cedar Bank: Amanda Cole (InfoSec), Diego Ramos (Procurement), Neda Khan (Legal), Tom Liu (Cloud)
summary: Walkthrough of SIG/CAIQ sections relevant to Cedar Bank's vendor risk process. Covered SOC 2 evidence, SSO/SAML & RBAC, audit logs and retention, encryption (KMS/HSM), data residency and network isolation for Redwood Private/Dedicated. Agreed next steps to share SOC 2 Type II, architecture/network diagrams, and a completed SIG spreadsheet; schedule follow-up deep dive with Cedar Cloud team next week.
topics: Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM details
transcript: [00:00] Marcus Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 55, 56 minutes on the calendar for the SIG walkthrough. Um Priya and I will lead, Oliver from CSM is here if you have contract questions.

[00:12] Amanda Cole: Great thanks Marcus. We opened a vendor risk ticket, and we've got about 80 SIG questions. We're mostly looking for SOC 2, access controls, encryption, and where things live - data residency.

[00:28] Priya Shah: Totally. We'll go section by section. Quick note - some of our names might come through wrong on the transcript, apologies in advance. We'll share a clean spreadsheet export with all answers and attachments.
[00:40] Diego Ramos: Timeline wise, procurement needs the filled SIG and evidence by next Thursday ideally, that's 11/13.

[00:48] Marcus Lee: Good to know, we'll prioritize that. First up: SOC 2 Type II. Redwood is SOC 2 Type II for our hosted API; we can provide a redacted report and cover letter. That's most of the compliance evidence customers ask for.
[01:05] Neda Khan: Is the report third-party audited? And do you allow customers to review the full report onsite or do you limit distribution?

[01:12] Oliver Grant: Yes third-party auditor. We typically provide a redacted PDF for NDAs; full report access can be arranged under a mutual NDA process. We'll include the redaction guidance in the doc we send.
[01:28] Amanda Cole: For encryption - we need details on KMS and key management. Are keys customer-managed? Any HSM integration?

[01:35] Priya Shah: Good question. For Redwood Hosted, we manage encryption keys in cloud KMS; for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM. We'll attach a KMS integration doc showing envelope encryption, key rotation policies and KMS access controls.
[01:54] Tom Liu: For private, do you support AWS KMS with CMKs in our account or do you require a proxy key store?

[02:00] Priya Shah: For Redwood Private in VPC mode we support using your AWS KMS CMKs - you can control the keys in your account. For Dedicated (reserved capacity) we have customer-managed KMS options as well, and we can provide HSM-backed keys on request.
[02:18] Amanda Cole: Audit logs - what level of detail do you capture, and how long retained? We need immutable logs for 12 months minimum.

[02:26] Marcus Lee: We capture token-level request metadata, user IDs tied to API keys, model version, latency and error codes. Default retention for hosted is 90 days but we offer extended retention as an add-on and for Dedicated/Private customers we can meet 12 months retention. We'll share a log schema and retention policy.
[02:45] Diego Ramos: Is there an exportable format for logs and can they be pushed into our SIEM?
[02:50] Priya Shah: Yes logs can be exported via S3 or syslog/forwarding to your SIEM in JSON; for Private you can keep logs inside your network and hook native SIEM. We'll include a sample log dump.
[03:05] Amanda Cole: Access control - RBAC and SSO. We use Okta, need SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO - can Redwood integrate?

[03:12] Marcus Lee: Absolutely. We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user management. Roles map to RBAC policies; for enterprise accounts we can onboard via your IdP. We have a doc with claims mapping and example SAML metadata.
[03:31] Neda Khan: Is there role separation for developers vs admins? We can't have developer access to billing or audit logs.
[03:37] Priya Shah: Yes roles are configurable. Out of the box we have Admin, Developer, Billing, Read-only Audit. You can request custom roles for separation of duties.
[03:50] Amanda Cole: Data residency - our regulator requires data to remain in US-only regions. How do you handle regional placement for hosted?

[03:58] Marcus Lee: By default we host in US and EU regions; you can pin your account to a region. For stricter needs we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private where resources are constrained to specified regions and network ACLs prevent cross-region egress. We'll share a region and data-flow diagram.
[04:20] Tom Liu: On networking - for private deployments does traffic terminate in our VPC and is there a private endpoint?

[04:26] Priya Shah: Yes Private deployments are customer-managed and can run inside your VPC; we provide connectors or an appliance image. For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private endpoints - we'll include architecture diagrams and network ACL examples.
[04:46] Amanda Cole: Incident response - do you have a playbook and SLA for breach notification? We need 72 hours notification if there's a confirmed data breach.

[04:53] Oliver Grant: We have an incident response plan and SOC contacts. We commit to regulator-required notification timelines; specifics are in our security program doc. We'll provide a redacted IR playbook and contact process.
[05:10] Diego Ramos: A few SIG items are about third-party subprocessors and subcontracts - can you provide a current list of subprocessors and whether you have data processing agreements in place?
[05:19] Marcus Lee: Yes, we'll attach a current subprocessor list and the DPA template. We maintain vendor assessments and can share evidence of their compliance status.
[05:32] Amanda Cole: Pen testing - do you allow us to run a third-party pen test, or do you publish recent pentest results?

[05:39] Priya Shah: We perform annual third-party pen tests and can share an executive summary. For customer-initiated pen tests, we typically coordinate scope and schedule; there's a process to avoid disruption. We'll include the pentest summary and the request process.

[05:56] Marcus Lee: A note on the SIG answers: some questions ask about model internals and training data. We answer operationally about inference and data retention - we do not disclose training datasets; also for hosted we do not use customer prompts to train models unless there's an explicit opt-in and contract term. We'll make that explicit in the SIG responses.
[06:15] Amanda Cole: Important for us - no prompt data used for training without consent. Please call that out in writing.
[06:20] Marcus Lee: Will do; we'll mark it clearly in the spreadsheet and SOC addendum.
[06:30] Tom Liu: A technical question: you mentioned KV cache and batching - do these affect PII exposure in logs or caches?

[06:37] Priya Shah: The KV cache is ephemeral in memory on the serving nodes and isn't persisted in logs. We do not persist prompt text in the cache longer than the request lifetime; for customers needing stricter guarantees we recommend Private where cache lifetime is controlled and nodes are in your network. We'll include a short note clarifying cache behavior.
[06:56] Neda Khan: For evidence attachments, can we get: SOC2 Type II redacted, KMS whitepaper, architecture/network diagrams, log schema, and the subprocessor list?
[07:03] Marcus Lee: Yes - we'll bundle those. Also we'll fill out the SIG spreadsheet column-by-column and flag anything that needs legal redlines. Expect an initial package by EOD 11/07.
[07:18] Diego Ramos: Good. Also we may request a live demo of Private deployment so our cloud team can vet EKS/VM images.
[07:24] Priya Shah: Happy to schedule a technical deep dive with our infra team and your cloud engineers - propose 60-90 minutes, we can demo VPC setup and KMS integration.

[07:36] Marcus Lee: Quick recap before we close: we'll share the filled SIG spreadsheet, SOC2 redacted, KMS/HSM docs, architecture diagrams, log export sample, and subprocessor list by 11/07. We'll schedule a follow-up technical deep dive with Tom and team next week. Any blockers on that timeline?
[07:54] Amanda Cole: That works. Procurement may want negotiated terms but the timeline is fine.
[08:02] Marcus Lee: Great. Oliver will follow up with calendar invites and attach the evidence bundle. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing with next steps.
[08:11] Oliver Grant: Thanks all - I'll add a note in the deal record with the evidence checklist and next meeting. Bye.
[08:15] Amanda Cole: Thanks bye.
